title: ر ز and the sibilants س ش
objectives: Student can identify and pronounce ر, ز, س, ش in isolation on sight.
Student can produce ر with the correct light tongue-tap quality (not a static English/Uzbek "r").
Student can distinguish ز from ذ (already taught) without collapsing them.

slides.heading: Lesson 1.3 — ر ز and the sibilants س ش
Cumulative recap — all 9 letters so far

audio.cue: ا: an open, unobstructed sound from deep in the chest cavity — no closure anywhere, just a clear open vowel
lips fully together
tongue-tip on gum ridge
tongue between teeth
ح: a strong, breathy, unvoiced friction from the middle of the throat — like fogging a mirror from deep in the throat, no English equivalent
خ: a rasping fricative from the upper throat/back of the tongue against the soft palate — a genuine back-of-throat 'kh', not softened
د: tongue-tip taps the upper gum ridge firmly — a plain, crisp 'd'
ذ: tongue-tip between the teeth, same point as ث but VOICED — 'th' as in 'this', never a 'z'

audio.cue: ش: middle of tongue against the roof of the mouth, a soft 'sh'

slides.makhraj: middle of tongue against the roof of the mouth

ش: middle of tongue against the roof of the mouth, a soft 'sh'

script: Open with a cumulative cold-call of all 9 letters learned so far before introducing ر.
Model ر as a single light tongue-flap, not a static English/Uzbek "r" — isolate the tongue-tap motion before asking for imitation.
Give ر dedicated correction time; Arabic101's own research flags it as unusually error-prone even among fluent readers.
Re-test the ز vs ذ collapse risk flagged in lesson 1.2 specifically for this student, not from memory.
Keep س/ش crisp even at speed — don't let rushed sibilants blur together.
listenFor: ر produced as a static, untapped English/Uzbek-style "r" instead of a light single flap — per Arabic101's own framing ("90% of RA mistakes happen here").
ز drifting toward ذ or vice versa — re-confirm the D→Z-family collapse pattern flagged in lesson 1.2 is (or isn't) present for this specific student (A.3).
س and ش losing crispness when said quickly back to back (rushed, blurred sibilants).
